The *Kusalattika, Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 4.7) is a canonical treatise situated within the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Methodologically, this section cross-analyzes conditional relations (*paccaya*) by coordinating the matrix of the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*) with the supplementary or concluding pairs (*piṭṭhiduka*) of the Abhidhamma mātikā [SuttaCentral].
No distinct parallels are recognized in non-Theravāda canons by SuttaCentral, reflecting the distinctive structural organization of the Theravāda *Paṭṭhāna* [SuttaCentral]. However, computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive intra-canonical formulaic reuse across the Abhidhamma, registering 6,498 matching passages across 233 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur with structurally contiguous and corresponding analytical sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, most prominently *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1; 900 matches), *Kusalattika, Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 4.3; 417 matches), *Tika Saraṇaduka* (Patthana 4.8; 364 matches), *Kusalattika, Āsavaparāmāsagocchaka* (Patthana 4.4; 329 matches), and the inverted combination *Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.13; 293 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects cross-language phraseological alignments with northern scholastic works, notably Vasubandhu's Sanskrit *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and its canonical Tibetan translation, alongside Tibetan versions of Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā-lakṣaṇānusāriṇī*, the *Karmaprajñapti*, and the *Munimatālaṃkāra* [DharmaNexus].
